name: Jason Kropf

name: Jason Kropf

name: Jason Kropf

name: Jason Kropf

name: Jason Kropf
reasoning: As co-chair of the Joint Committee on Addiction and Community Safety Response he personally floor-carried HB 4002 (2024R1), the Measure 110 rewrite, whose central mechanism is police contact followed by deflection into assessment and treatment rather than jail, and he described that operating model at the January 2024 news conference unveiling the framework. He also floor-carried HB 2005 (2025R1) broadening the standard for when a person is in need of treatment as a danger to self or others, and chief-sponsored HB 3069 (2025R1), which reorganizes existing Criminal Justice Commission grants into a Public Safety Coordination Grant Program and an Oregon Law Enforcement Grant Program rather than expanding them. Keeping police as first responders while adding a behavioral health and addiction pathway is chair 3; he did not shift non-violent calls to unarmed co-responders (chair 2) or press for increased police staffing, equipment and pay (chair 4).
